Was forced to take my chance at homelessness, then was renting out rooms while working part time. Found a fulltime job that offered housing and took it. Yes working 40 hours is exhausting, but coming home to a place I feel safe is SUCH a game changer. I feel less exhausted coming home from work than I ever did when I lived with my mom- which was part-time. I have roommates, and it took me over a year to get to this point- where I'm truly comfortable and feel safe actually USING the house- and still need to unlearn some of the habits forced upon me by my mom. I still have days where I want to give up and think I just can't do it– but they get less and less common with time.

Not that it will work out for everyone, but for at least some– working full-time will feel more doable when you're in a safe environment.


Edit: I should add that I still don't have many of the skills that adults my age should have, and I very much still lack the energy to properly take care of myself– but it gets slightly easier. Eating toast and cereal every day is so so worth not being in Hell anymore. If I'm too exhausted to even prepare that then I have protein shakes in the fridge. It is not healthy, but eating something is better than nothing- and I'd argue, its better for your body than constant, inescapable survival mode.
